question: Why doesn't a lump of ordinary matter collapse under the electric attractions inside it?
answer: Because electrons refuse to share a state. Freeman Dyson and Andrew Lenard proved in 1967 that electric forces alone cannot keep bulk matter stable; Pauli's rule barring two electrons from one quantum state is what holds it up. Without it, binding energy would outgrow the amount of matter: merging two lumps would release an explosion.
move: A rule about what cannot happen can hold up more than any force.
reference: Dyson & Lenard, Stability of Matter. I, Journal of Mathematical Physics 8, 423, 1967
